Interface DataKeyProvider

All Known Implementing Classes:
JceDataKeyProvider
public interface DataKeyProvider
SPI for envelope-encryption key management, implemented by consumers against an in-process key store or a remote KMS (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, GCP Cloud KMS, etc.).

newDataKey maps onto operations such as AWS KMS GenerateDataKey or Vault transit/datakey/plaintext, which return a plaintext data-encryption key (DEK) and its wrapped form in one round trip. GCP Cloud KMS has no equivalent data-key operation; its documented envelope pattern is to generate the DEK locally and then call Encrypt to wrap it, which is likewise a single round trip performed entirely inside newDataKey() — implementors targeting GCP are using this SPI as intended. unwrap maps onto the corresponding KMS decrypt operation.

Security contract (normative)

unwrap receives a keyId and wrapped blob read from unauthenticated ciphertext: the GCM tag cannot be verified until the DEK has been recovered, so at the time of this call both arguments are attacker-controlled. Implementations MUST:

  • pass the supplied keyId to the KMS as the key restriction for the decrypt operation (e.g. the KeyId parameter of AWS KMS Decrypt) — never let the wrapped blob itself select which key is used to unwrap it; and
  • reject any keyId outside the set of key-encryption keys (KEKs) the application intends to trust.

Without both of these, an attacker who knows the plaintext of any DEK wrapped under any KEK the application is permitted to decrypt can forge messages that verify. Callers such as EnvelopeCodec additionally enforce an allowlist before invoking unwrap; this contract exists so that a provider used outside such a caller is not silently unsafe on its own.

Caching contract

Implementations MAY cache unwrap results, keyed by (keyId, hash(wrapped)) — where the hash is collision-resistant (e.g. SHA-256) — or by the wrapped bytes themselves, to avoid a network round trip per decode. Any such cache MUST be bounded in both entries and time.

Error contract

unwrap MUST throw DecryptionException only when the underlying KMS or JCE layer has affirmatively rejected the blob as invalid (e.g. an integrity-check failure). Failures that do not assert the blob is invalid — timeouts, throttling, credential expiry, or any other availability failure — MUST instead propagate as other runtime exceptions, which callers are expected to distinguish from an affirmative rejection (e.g. by wrapping them as KeyAccessException). Conflating the two would turn a transient key-infrastructure outage into data loss for a caller that quarantines or discards on DecryptionException.

Thread-safety

Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use: a single provider instance is shared across both encode and decode paths, potentially from multiple threads at once.

  • Method Details

    • newDataKey

      DataKey newDataKey()
      Generates a fresh data-encryption key and returns it wrapped under this provider's current key-encryption key.
      Returns:
      a new DataKey carrying the plaintext key and its wrapped form

    • unwrap

      SecretKey unwrap(String keyId, byte[] wrapped)
      Recovers the plaintext data-encryption key from its wrapped form.

      See the security, caching, and error contracts on this interface: both parameters are attacker-controlled at the time of this call.

      Parameters:
      keyId - identifies which key-encryption key was used to wrap the data key
      wrapped - the wrapped data-encryption key bytes
      Returns:
      the recovered plaintext key

    • allowsKeyId

      default boolean allowsKeyId(String keyId)
      Returns whether this provider is willing to unwrap data keys wrapped under the given key id.

      This is the provider's own admission check. The default implementation allows every key id; implementations backed by a fixed set of trusted keys (such as a Map of KEKs) should override this to reject any key id outside that set.

      Parameters:
      keyId - the key id to evaluate
      Returns:
      true if this provider will unwrap data keys under keyId
